text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALES - Moldova bought 34,000 tonnes of PL-480 hard red winter wheat. The wheat was sold by Farmland Industries at $180.99 a tonne, FOB, Texas Gulf. Shipment was slated for October 10-25.

RICE SALE - Moldova bought 13,309 tonnes of PL-480 U.S. No. 2 long grain milled rice. It bought 2,600 tonnes from Louis Dreyfus at $406.28 a tonne, free alongside (FAS), U.S. Gulf; 1,500 from Garnac Grain at $405.65 and 9,209.50 from Continental Grain at $408.84. Shipment is for November 1-25.

WHEAT TENDERS - Surinam will be seeking to purchase 2,800 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better northern spring/dark northern spring wheat in bulk under the PL 480 Title I. Shipment is set for October 10-25. Bids must be submitted by September 26.

- The Commodity Credit Corp of USDA said it did not buy any wheat in its tender Friday for Eritrea. The CCC had sought about 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 or better hard red winter, soft red winter or soft white wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment was to be Oct 10-Nov 5. No reason was given for not buying the wheat.

WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka will seek on October 18 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat. It said 50,000 tonnes would be soft white wheat and 50,000 tonnes hard red winter wheat for November 11-20 shipment.
- Pakistan will tender Sunday for 200,000 tonnes U.S.grade 2 or better soft white wheat under the GSM-102 program for October 10-31 shipment, its U.S. export agent said.

- Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 is the final date for offers. Confirmation is set for October 2.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDERS - Taiwanese buyers are expected to hold four tenders for a total of 104,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 88,000 tonnes of corn next week, traders said. State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp may seek 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans for shipment from the U.S. Gulf from October 25 to November 10.

RICE TENDERS - Sri Lanka was to decide Friday on awarding a 50,000-tonne rice tender, the state buying arm Cooperative Wholesale Establishment (CWE) said. Forty one exporters have responded to a Sri Lankan government tender for 50,000 tonnes of rice for October/November delivery.
RICE TENDERS - Moldova will tender Wednesday for 14,000 tonnes of PL-480 long-grain milled rice for November.

MARKET TALK - USDA offered Brazil $150 million in GSM-102 credit guarantees for fiscal 1997. It also offered $80 million to East Caribbean countries, and $40 million to the West Caribbean. Brazil's amount included $75 million for wheat, cotton, rice, feed grains, breeder livestock, poultry breeder stock, poultry breeder stock, fresh fruit, hops, tallow, meat, peanuts and other commodities. The balance was not allocated. USDA offered $20 million to Tunisia, $15 million to India, $12 million to Croatia, and $1.5 million to Lithuania.

MARKET TALK - U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday he will resume Export Enhancement Program subsidies if necessary, but said USDA has no contingency plan to do so on paper yet. Also, U.S. grain market analysts said there is no need for the U.S. Agriculture Department to soon resume EEP subsidies for wheat.
